chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Lester Young's different sound and what Cootie learned
summary: Even then Lester was unlike Hawkins and unlike anyone Cootie had heard; Cootie learned some syncopations from him.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: I see. Well, was he -- was he blowing so much then?
But was it different? It wasn't like Hawk. Or was it?
No, no. It wasn't like no Hawk.
And he still had that different concept, huh?
So he really was an innovator with that concept, wasn't he?
Yeah. That's what made me wanted to go with them.
Because he was different from anybody I ever heard.
Is that right? That's very funny, because
in a way, the style that -- well, I mean the style -- your idol was Louis.
And Lester was playing a style that was coming after the style that Louis established. Am I right in thinking that?
Well, yeah. He was a stylist.
And he was the next person I'd ever heard in person.
He was the greatest thing I'd ever heard in person.
Yeah. Right. Yeah. He was the biggest talent you'd come across personally.
Yeah. Cause he had a different feel for the beat, didn't he.
Yeah. And I wanted to learn something about it.
And did you pick up that feel?
Yeah, I learned something from him.
In the beat, in different syncopations that he had.
Did -- well, he was what, like five years older than you?
